title: Introduce local-failover-bridge-and-staggered-rollback-for-private-deployments
author: Marco Chen
description: Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private reported a single-node maintenance cycle caused cascading service disruption in edge clusters because egress routing was rebalanced synchronously and rollbacks were applied cluster-wide. This PR introduces a local-failover-bridge component that provides per-node ephemeral routing during maintenance and a staggered-rollback controller to avoid global reinstatement storms. The goal is to allow controlled failover inside customer VPCs and provide safe rollback semantics with telemetry-driven delays. Design: - local-failover-bridge: a lightweight sidecar that advertises temporary egress endpoints and proxies KV cache warming traffic during node maintenance; integrates with existing health probes and supports a sticky-lease for prefetched KV. - staggered-rollback-controller: orchestrates rollback in windows using a jittered, telemetry-anchored schedule; honors SLO budgets and will abort if latency or error-rate thresholds breach configured limits. - Telemetry hooks: new metrics for rollback_progress, bridge_failover_count, and rollback_abort_reasons. - Config: installer changes add new flags in values.yaml to enable per-cluster policies and a safe default off for upgrades. Checklist: - [x] Implement bridge sidecar and control hooks - [x] Add staggered rollback controller + unit tests - [x] Add telemetry and alerts - [x] Integration smoke tests in CI - [x] Docs: installer notes and upgrade guidance Migration notes: enabling the bridge requires adding a 'bridgePolicy' section to the private installer config; backward compatible if omitted. See docs/installer/local-failover.md for details. Related: addresses ENG-1746 and SUP-4421. Testing: local integration against three-node on-prem cluster; CI ran smoke and e2e with a canary rollout simulation. Risks: bridging introduces a new network hop — we limit this to maintenance windows and recommend enabling only when node-level maintenance is planned. Rollback controller uses conservative defaults but can be tuned per-customer.
